chosen.premise: Slowpoke’s tail can break off without pain, then grow back without Slowpoke even noticing.
chosen.hook: Slowpoke can lose its tail and not notice when it comes back.
chosen.visualIdea: Use a before-and-after tail silhouette: attached, missing, then regrown while Slowpoke remains expressionless.
chosen.note: A distinctly Slowpoke biological oddity with a clear three-beat visual: tail attached, missing, then regrown while Slowpoke remains unaware.

candidates.premise: Some places worship Slowpoke because they believe every one of its yawns makes it rain.
candidates.hook: Some people worship Slowpoke for one absurd weather prediction.
candidates.visualIdea: Build from a Slowpoke yawn to dark clouds, rainfall, and a crowd bowing to it.
candidates.note: Very surprising and visually theatrical, though the belief is less mechanically concrete because the Pokédex only reports worship based on the tradition.

candidates.premise: Slowpoke fishes with its tail, but often forgets what it is doing and loafs by the river all day.
candidates.hook: Slowpoke has a fishing strategy—and immediately forgets it is fishing.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate a sweetened tail luring prey, then cut to Slowpoke staring blankly beside the river.
candidates.note: Strongly supported and easy to animate, with a funny contradiction between an effective fishing tactic and immediate forgetfulness.

candidates.premise: Slowpoke can take five seconds to feel pain after an attack, making its sluggishness a literal delay.
candidates.hook: Slowpoke gets hurt—but its body takes five seconds to notice.
candidates.visualIdea: Show an attack landing, then freeze Slowpoke for five seconds before a delayed pain reaction.
candidates.note: A concrete, highly visual mechanic, but the research also gives conflicting delays of five seconds and an entire day, weakening the premise if not carefully framed.

candidates.premise: Slowpoke has two stage-two evolutions: one requires level 37, the other a trade while holding a King's Rock.
candidates.hook: Slowpoke can evolve two ways—but the rules could not be more different.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen into Slowbro’s level-37 path and Slowking’s trade-with-item path.
candidates.note: Excellent rule comparison and screen structure, but evolution-method explainers are familiar and the methods rely on trusted secondary research.

candidates.premise: Regular Slowpoke is Water/Psychic, while its Galar variety is Psychic-only at the same height and weight.
candidates.hook: Same Slowpoke size, different typing: Galar takes away its Water type.
candidates.visualIdea: Place the two forms side by side with matching size stats while the Water type visibly disappears.
candidates.note: The matching height and weight make a clean comparison, but regional typing changes are common and the reveal is less emotionally or narratively distinctive.

rounds.request: None needed; the chosen angle is already specific, surprising, highly visual, and fully supported. Stronger alternatives would need an equally concrete Slowpoke-only rule or contradiction.
